thread.title: Spotify Implies Apple, Google Stifling Competition: Macquarie - Wiredfocus

title: Spotify Implies Apple, Google Stifling Competition: Macquarie - Wiredfocus
text:
Spotify Implies Apple, Google Stifling Competition: Macquarie April 17, 2018 
Updated April 17, 2018 2:47 p.m. ET 
Apple ( AAPL ) and Alphabet ’s ( GOOGL ) Google unit both have a problem with their dominance of mobile technology: they’re giving the impression they’re hampering competition. 
In a note to clients today, Ben Schachter with Macquarie Research reiterates his Outperform rating on Apple shares, but also describes being troubled by a detail in the IPO prospectus of Spotify Technology ( SPOT ), the streaming music company that went public on April 3. Its music service competes with Apple’s Apple Music and with Google’s Google Play Music , among others. 
Both those companies control the mobile devices on which Spotify depends for distribution, and they charge fees for it, something Spotify noted and that concerns Schachter: 
In its public filing, Spotify states that AAPL and GOOG are leaving others at a competitive disadvantage by charging in-app platform fees while exempting their own music streaming services. Statements like these make us more nervous about AAPL and GOOG being open to liability/regulation as they add additional services that directly compete with app developers paying to be on the platforms. This is an area to watch. 
He notes it’s getting harder to justify the app fees of the duo given they are increasingly in direct competition with their developers: 
While in the past, the 30% fee from the App Store and Google Play could have been considered simply a fee that must be paid to reach customers on those platforms, with music plans from AAPL and GOOG, as well as video and other potential services, competitors such as Spotify may be able to draw more attention to the fact that competitor services will be structurally more expensive to consumers than those from AAPL and GOOG (and even potentially AMZN) because of the fee. Some might try to argue that this is anti- competitive and harmful to consumers. 
Spotify has said Apple Music is its closest competitor in streaming music, with Spotify having 159 million total monthly average users, of which 71 million are paying subscribers . Apple recently disclosed Apple Music has 40 million paying users. READ You Can Now Visit DISNEY PARKS on Google Maps 
The question of profit margin and fees for Spotify is particularly interesting because most of Schachter’s note is about the business model of Apple Music. Schachter finds that Apple Music, at 40 million users, is “likely the fastest growing contributor to Services revenues” for Apple. 
However, it is not the biggest contributor to profit, he emphasizes. “Its margin profile (we are modeling 15%) is fundamentally different to the App Store (estimated 90% gross margin), and as such Music will likely never be a direct meaningful contributor to profits,” concludes Schachter. 
By 2020, writes Schachter, “Music will contribute less than 4% of Services gross profit, versus apps at 56%.” He thinks investors shouldn’t be alarmed, but they should pay attention to the higher-profit App Store.
